Find the unknown functions $f(t)$ and $g(t)$ in the general solution to the system, shown below.

$$
x(t)={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}f(t) \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡t\end{aligned}]+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}g(t) \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡t\end{aligned}]
$$

*Hint: One of the eigenvalues of the matrix is ${\lambda }_{1}=\text{i}.$*

worked_solution:
We need to find the eigenvalues and associated eigenvectors of the matrix 

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

We are given that the eigenvalue is ${\lambda }_{1}=\text{i}.$ 

Let's go through the process of finding the eigenvectors. For ${\lambda }_{1}=\text{i},$ we get 

$$
A-{\lambda }_{1}I=[\begin{aligned}-\text{i} & 1 \\ -1 & -\text{i}\end{aligned}]∼[\begin{aligned}1 & \text{i} \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

So, we get an eigenvector 
${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}-\text{i} \\ 1\end{aligned}].$

**Note:** The eigenvector corresponding to the second eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{2}={\overset{―}{\lambda }}_{1}$ is 
${v}_{2}={\overset{―}{v}}_{1}.$ But we do not require this eigenvector for solving our system.

The solution that we obtain for the eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{1}=\text{i}$ and its associated eigenvector is

$$
{x}_{1}(t)=[\begin{aligned}-\text{i} \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{\text{i}t}.
$$

We now express this as a real function. Using Euler's formula, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}(t) & =[\begin{aligned}-\text{i} \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{\text{i}t} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-\text{i} \\ 1\end{aligned}]\cdot (\operatorname{cos}⁡t+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡t) \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-\text{i}\operatorname{cos}⁡t+\operatorname{sin}⁡t \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡t+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡t\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡t-\text{i}\operatorname{cos}⁡t \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡t+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡t\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡t \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡t\end{aligned}]+\text{i}[\begin{aligned}-\operatorname{cos}⁡t \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡t\end{aligned}] \\  & ={\text{w}}_{1}(t)+\text{i}{\text{w}}_{2}(t).\end{aligned}
$$

The vectors ${w}_{1}$ and ${w}_{2}$ are linearly independent. Therefore, the general solution of the system is

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{x}(t) & ={c}_{1}{\text{w}}_{1}(t)+{c}_{2}{\text{w}}_{2}(t) \\  & ={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡t \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡t\end{aligned}]+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}-\operatorname{cos}⁡t \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡t\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, 

$$
f(t)=\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,g(t)=-\operatorname{cos}⁡t.
$$

EXPLANATION

We need to find the eigenvalues and associated eigenvectors of the matrix

A=[01−10].

We are given that the eigenvalue is λ1=i.

Let's go through the process of finding the eigenvectors. For λ1=i, we get A−λ1I=[−i1−1−i]∼[1i00]. So, we get an eigenvector v1=[−i1].

Note: The eigenvector corresponding to the second eigenvalue λ2=λ―1 is v2=v―1. But we do not require this eigenvector for solving our system.

The solution that we obtain for the eigenvalue λ1=i and its associated eigenvector is x1(t)=[−i1]eit.

We now express this as a real function. Using Euler's formula, we obtain x1(t)=[−i1]eit=[−i1]⋅(cos⁡t+isin⁡t)=[−icos⁡t+sin⁡tcos⁡t+isin⁡t]=[sin⁡t−icos⁡tcos⁡t+isin⁡t]=[sin⁡tcos⁡t]+i[−cos⁡tsin⁡t]=w1(t)+iw2(t).

The vectors w1 and w2 are linearly independent. Therefore, the general solution of the system is x(t)=c1w1(t)+c2w2(t)=c1[sin⁡tcos⁡t]+c2[−cos⁡tsin⁡t].

Finally, f(t)=sin⁡t,g(t)=−cos⁡t.
